Subject: HIPAA / BAA eligibility and deployment options for MedWise - post-call recap

Hi Ashley / Dr. Patel —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

- Use case summary: MedWise will be using the API to summarize and classify clinical notes (patient names, MRNs, diagnosis codes). You noted these are PHI and would like to understand options for a BAA and where PHI can be processed/stored.
- Questions we promised to follow up on: Redwood's BAA availability, which deployment modes are eligible for PHI, data retention defaults, and what information we need to complete the vendor security questionnaire.

Attachments: HIPAA_BAA_FAQ_v2.pdf, vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (draft) — please review at a high level.

High-level answers: 
- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for customers processing PHI. In most cases BAAs are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted (multi-tenant) customers we handle on a case-by-case basis; we typically require additional controls and legal review.
- Deployment options: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem) are the primary recommended modes for PHI workloads because they provide stronger tenant isolation and customer-managed networking.
- SOC 2: We maintain SOC 2 controls across our platform; I can share the SOC 2 report under NDA if that helps your security team.

Next steps / asks: 
1) Can you confirm the types of PHI (e.g., patient identifiers, full notes, images) and whether any data will be uploaded in batch (S3) vs. live API calls?
2) Please have your security contact (security@medwisehealth.com) review the attached questionnaire and flag any questions.
3) Would you like a draft BAA to review? We can share a redlineable draft via DocuSign.

Looping in Neha (solutions) and Michael (CS) to support the technical questionnaire and BAA process.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility and deployment options for MedWise - technical follow-up

Hi all — following up with technical notes. I opened the attached redwood-security-overview.pdf and included a few clarifications inline below.

1) SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. We can share the report under an NDA; I'll coordinate with legal to provision it to MedWise security.

2) BAA availability: We execute BAAs for customers processing PHI. Recommended deployment modes for PHI are Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem). For Hosted (multi-tenant) customers, a BAA can occasionally be supported but requires additional controls (customer-specific isolation, strict retention/deletion agreements, legal review) and is evaluated case-by-case. For most production PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private.

3) Data retention / PHI handling: 
- Default behavior: short-lived KV/prefix caches used for latency; full request/response logs are retained per customer retention policy. For PHI workloads we support configurable retention windows and can configure automatic deletion and minimized logging.
- Deletion workflow: retention policy enforcement, secure deletion jobs, and audit logs are available. We will document the retention window and deletion SLA in the BAA and account agreement.

4) KMS / encryption: 
- Encryption at rest: all customer data at rest is encrypted.
- BYOK: for Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys; BYOK may be available under certain enterprise agreements.

5) Batch ingestion vs. live API: both supported. For batch S3 ingestion we recommend Dedicated or Private to keep S3 endpoints within your VPC (or use private peering). Live API calls can be routed to Dedicated capacity with per-customer isolation to meet PHI requirements.

6) Next items we need from MedWise to proceed: 
- Estimated monthly call volume and average tokens per call (rough numbers are fine).
- Confirmation of PHI categories and whether any data should be redacted at source.
- Security questionnaire completed (see attached).

I'll prepare a short tech appendix for the BAA covering retention, deletion SLA, KMS options, and network isolation. I can also draft a sample BAA for review.

Regards,
